carousel.cover_headline:
Regenerative Agriculture:
Restoring Soil, Not Just
Maintaining It

slides.label: WHAT IT IS
slides.headline: Regenerative farming restores soil health and biodiversity
slides.insight: It goes beyond maintaining land — it actively rehabilitates ecosystems.

slides.label: THE DEBATE
slides.headline: **No universally accepted definition** exists yet for regenerative agriculture
slides.insight: No global criteria or regulatory framework has been agreed upon.

slides.label: WHAT'S PROPOSED
slides.headline: Proposed benefits span soil, climate, food quality and human health
slides.insight: Scientists say more evidence is still needed to confirm these links.

slides.label: WHY IT MATTERS
slides.headline: Outcomes vary across crops, environments and farm sizes
slides.insight: What works on one farm may not work on another — context matters.

slides.label: TRY THIS WEEK
slides.headline: Look up one regenerative farming practice used near you
slides.insight: Composting, cover crops and mulching are common starting points.

sources: Institute for the Advancement of Food and Nutrition Sciences (IAFNS), 2026 (reported by Newswise)
carousel.caption:
Regenerative agriculture restores soil health and biodiversity — not just maintains it.

Scientists say the approach shows promise across soil, food quality and human health.
But there is still no agreed global definition or framework — and more evidence is needed.
What does "growing food naturally" mean to you?

Sources: Institute for the Advancement of Food and Nutrition Sciences (IAFNS), 2026 (Newswise)
